pr_title: ENH: Add na_value argument to DataFrame.to_numpy
pr_body:
- [x] closes #33820
- [x] tests added / passed
- [x] passes `black pandas`
- [x] passes `git diff upstream/master -u -- "*.py" | flake8 --diff`
- [x] whatsnew entry
pr_comments:
Another interesting issue is the behavior for mixed numeric and non-numeric data types. In the docstring we say that these will promote to object, which does happen but apparently numpy decides to convert the datetime to int beforehand anyways (we get the expected output if we explicitly ask for object):
```python
[ins] In [1]: df = pd.DataFrame({"A": [1, 2], "B": [3.0, 4.5]})                                                                                                                                              

[ins] In [2]: df['C'] = pd.date_range('2000', periods=2)                                                                                                                                                     

[ins] In [3]: df.to_numpy()                                                                                                                                                                                  
Out[3]: 
array([[1, 3.0, 946684800000000000],
       [2, 4.5, 946771200000000000]], dtype=object)

[ins] In [4]: df.to_numpy(dtype=object)                                                                                                                                                                      
Out[4]: 
array([[1, 3.0, Timestamp('2000-01-01 00:00:00')],
       [2, 4.5, Timestamp('2000-01-02 00:00:00')]], dtype=object)
```

So I think you need to deal with this deeper into the internals, as I mentioned before. It is there that the custom pandas logic to decide on the resulting dtype is done (which is indeed different from numpy's result dtype)

Check BlockManager.as_array -> this also already handles the case of a single Block (to keep the no copy behaviour there).

I think we can expand that method to support na_value

issue_context.title: ENH: Add na_value to DataFrame.to_numpy
issue_context.body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Control the NA value used when converting a DataFrame to an ndarray.

#### Describe the solution you'd like

Add an `na_value` argument to `DataFrame.to_numpy()`. Has the same meaning as `na_value` in `Series.to_numpy`, except it applies to all the columns.

#### Additional context

```python
In [8]: df = pd.DataFrame({"A": pd.array([1, None])})

In [9]: df.to_numpy(na_value=np.nan)
```

This has come up in a few places (cc @jorisvandenbossche @dsaxton)
comments:
Thanks @TomAugspurger. https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/33809 took the approach of using DataFrame.astype(float).to_numpy() to coerce NA to np.nan which should likely be fixed once this becomes available.
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/8aa707298428801199280b2b994632080591700a/pandas/core/frame.py#L7873

review_comments: is this tested / hit at all? (the dtype part)
The added `test_to_numpy_dataframe_single_block` should cover this line I think

Can you add some more tests for a few "realistic" cases? Like a dataframe with nullable integer array (as mentioned above I think this will still fail) converting to float with np.nan as missing value, or converting to int with -1 as missing value.

Suggestion: pass through this `na_value` to `_interleave`, and then when looping over the blocks, you can check for ExtensionBlocks and then call `to_numpy` with the appropriate dtype and na_value. 

The lines above will need to be kept for non-EAs, but I think for EAs, we want to use their `to_numpy` implemenation, as this can potentially be more efficient in depending on the dtype/na_value combination

Pushed a change to make this update. In the single extension block case we're still doing a conversion to object (got several odd failures when I tried making the associated edit there) but I'm thinking this is already going to be a pretty inexpensive case anyways

> In the single extension block case we're still doing a conversion to object 

I think in the above `is self._is_single_block` checks, you can add an additional case for single ExtensionBlock (like there is already a check for single datetimetz block)
Got mixed up by the "blocks are transposed" thing and was missing a reshape, should be working now 🤞
This had to change because now the output array is a view, but only on the transpose of itself (which is a copy of the original data)

Good idea. Not sure if it's "bad style" but is another option simply to create a "should_copy" variable and update it for the interleave case? Might be a bit more explicit what we're thinking and helps avoid nested conditionals.
Such a variable is also fine, whatever is easiest to implement / you prefer
